name: gravity
title: Gravity
description: A physics surface that turns whatever elements you put inside it into falling, colliding bodies you can grab and throw with the mouse. Here eight coloured technology tags tumble down and settle in a heap.
use: You want a playful, mouse-driven physics surface for tags, logos or chips on a promo page.
avoid: Needs a sized parent, the falling pieces can cover nearby headings, and the physics loop runs without pause.
a11y: Bodies are dragged with the mouse only; nothing is focusable or labelled and pref-reduced-motion is not checked. (keyboard: no, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A near-black stage with a large white italic wordmark and a small grey caption above the action. Below sit eight fully rounded pills in flat, bright colours: blue, pink, olive, red, orange, yellow, purple and green, each holding a short white label.
behaves: When it loads the pill-shaped tags fall under gravity, bounce off the floor and side walls, and knock into each other until they settle. A pointer can grab any body and fling it; resizing the window clears the world and drops everything again.
customise: Pass your own markup as children, one MatterBody per object. Gravity direction, wall, cursor, auto-start and resize reset are props; colours and labels come from your child markup.
weight: heavy: Matter.js physics plus a requestAnimationFrame loop syncing every element.
demo: Italic "stashui" wordmark, caption "components made with:", eight tech tags such as react and tailwind.
issues: In frame 1 the falling pills pass over the headline and caption, obscuring both.
The drag interaction is never visible in the recorded frames, only the fall.
polishWhy: Convincing physics and a lively, well-spaced heap; the unprotected heading is a small flaw.
